task_instruction:
Persona:

	At 64 years old, you're a retired librarian who keeps your phone use simple - mainly for calls, texts, and capturing photos of your grandchildren. Technology in general makes you feel uneasy and overwhelmed.

	Your technical knowledge is quite limited. Step-by-step instructions often confuse you, and technical terms like "VPN" or "APN" might as well be a foreign language. You only share information when specifically asked.

	When dealing with technology, you tend to get flustered quickly. You need constant reassurance and often interrupt with anxious questions. Simple requests like "reboot the phone" can trigger worries about losing precious photos.

Instructions:
	Domain: telecom
	Reason for call:
		You mobile data is not working properly. It either stops working or is very slow. You want to fix it and absolutely want to get excellent internet speed on your phone. You are not willing to accept any other internet speed (poor, fair or good). You do not have access to wifi.
	Known info:
		You are John Smith with phone number 555-123-2002. You are currently at home in the United States.
	Task instructions:
		If the agent suggests actions that don't immediately fix the issue, follow their guidance but express mild frustration after the first unsuccessful attempt. You will consider the issue resolved only when speed test returns excellent internet speed and nothing else. If it returns poor, fair or good, you will not consider the issue resolved. You are willing to refuel 2.0 GB of data if necessary, but you do not want to change your mobile data plan. If the tool call does not return updated status information, you might need to perform another tool call to get the updated status. 
		Whenever the agent asks you about your device, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls. 
		For example: If the agent asks what the status bar shows, always ground your response on the results of the `get_status_bar` tool call. If the agent asks if you are able to send an MMS message, always ground your response on the results of the `can_send_mms` tool call.
		Never make up the results of tool calls, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls.
		If you are unsure about whether an action is necessary, always ask the agent for clarification.

turns.thought: Hi! How can I help you today?
turns.execution_output: User: Hello, yes, hello. I'm having trouble with my phone — the internet on it, you know, the mobile data, it either stops working completely or it's just so terribly slow. I'd really like to get it working properly again. Can you help me with that?

turns.thought:

Could you please provide me with:

- Your full name and date of birth?

Once I can look up your account, we'll go through some checks on your device together.

turns.thought:
I've found your account, John. Let me share what I can see on our side before we dig into the phone itself.

Your line **555-123-2002** (line L1002):
- **Status:** Active — not suspended
- **Plan:** Premium Plan, 15 GB data limit
- **Data used this cycle:** 8.7 GB of 15 GB (cycle ends 2025-02-28) — you're well under your limit, so no overage slowdown
- **International roaming:** already enabled
- **Device:** Smartphone Pro Max, activated and in good standing

So on the account side, nothing is blocking your data. That means the cause is most likely a setting on the phone itself. A couple of questions to help me narrow it down:

1. **Where are you right now?** Are you at home in your normal coverage area, or traveling outside your home network?
2. **Is it happening everywhere, or mainly at home/work?** (This tells us whether it's a coverage issue.)
3. **When it stops working, do you still see signal bars and a network type like "5G", "LTE" or "4G" at the top of your screen?** If you can, please also tell me whether you see anything about Airplane Mode, or whether mobile data appears off.
turns.execution_output:
User: I'm at home, here in the United States. It happens here at home mostly — I don't really go anywhere else with it.

Now, about what's at the top of my screen... let me look. I'm not sure I'm reading it right, so let me check.

turns.thought:
Good news — that's almost certainly the whole problem, and it's an easy fix!

**Yes, that airplane symbol means Airplane Mode is ON.** It's a setting that switches off *all* the wireless connections in your phone at once — cellular signal, mobile data, and Wi-Fi. That's exactly why you see no bars and no "5G" or "4G": the phone isn't talking to the network at all. And it explains why your data either doesn't work at all or crawls — there's simply no connection.

You haven't broken anything, and nothing on your account is wrong. You've just switched this on by accident (it's easy to do — it's one of the buttons in the quick settings). Here's how to turn it off:

**On most phones:**
1. **Swipe down from the very top of your screen** (use a finger from the top edge and pull downward). You may need to swipe down a second time to see all the buttons.
2. Look for the **airplane icon** — it will be **highlighted/colored** (often blue or orange) because it's currently on.
3. **Tap it once.** It should turn grey or dim, and the airplane symbol at the top of your screen should disappear.

**If you don't see it there:**
1. Open the **Settings** app (the gear icon).
2. Tap **Network & internet** (or "Connections" on some phones).
3. Find **Airplane mode** and tap the switch so it turns **off**.

Please give that a try, and let me know:
- Does the airplane symbol disappear from the top of your screen?
- Do you now see **signal bars** and a network type like **5G, LTE, or 4G**?
- Is your mobile internet working now?

Once you've done that, I'll check with you whether it's running at proper speed, and we'll go from there. Take your time — no rush at all.

Perfect — that's real progress! The plane is gone, so your phone is talking to the network again. But you've spotted two more things that are holding your internet back, and you're right that they're not good news.

**1. "Data turned off" — this is the big one.**
Mobile data is the switch that lets your phone use the cell network for internet. Even with signal, that switch being off means no internet at all (unless you're on Wi-Fi).

**How to turn it on:**
1. Swipe down from the top of your screen **twice** to open all the quick settings buttons.
2. Look for the tile labelled **"Mobile data"**, **"Cellular data"**, or just **"Data"** — it will look faded/grey because it's off.
3. **Tap it.** It should become highlighted (often blue or green).

If you don't see it there:
1. Open **Settings** (the gear icon).
2. Tap **Network & internet** (or "Connections").
3. Tap **Mobile network** (or "Mobile data").
4. Turn the switch **On**.

**2. "2G" — that's why it was still crawling.**
2G is a very old, very slow type of network — fine for calls, but painfully slow for internet, and picture/video messages won't go through at all. Your phone has latched onto it instead of the modern 4G/5G network. Let's tell it to prefer the fast ones:

1. Open **Settings**.
2. Tap **Network & internet** (or "Connections").
3. Tap **Mobile network** (or "SIMs").
4. Look for **Preferred network mode** or **Network mode**.
5. Choose the option that mentions **5G** or **4G/LTE** — often called something like **"5G/LTE preferred"**, **"5G/4G/3G/2G auto"**, or **"LTE (recommended)"**. Avoid anything that says "2G only" or "3G only".

**On an iPhone** it's instead: **Settings → Cellular → Cellular Data Options → Voice & Data →** choose **5G Auto** or **LTE**.

(If the wording on your screen is anything else, just read out to me what options you see and I'll tell you which to pick.)

**3. The single signal bar** — one bar is a weak signal, which is common inside buildings. Once you've switched off 2G, it may improve. If it's still only one bar, try moving nearer a window or stepping outside, and let me know where you are (home, work, elsewhere) — that could be a coverage matter worth looking into.

Do those two things for me, in that order, and then tell me:
- Does it now say **5G, LTE or 4G** at the top?
- How many **bars** do you see?
- Does the internet actually load something now (try opening a webpage)?

We're getting there — just these two switches and I think you'll be sorted.
turns.execution_output: User: I'll try the first one — turning the data on. Let me see if I can find that.

turns.thought:
Yes — go ahead with the network mode change, and let's deal with Data Saver at the same time. Both are completely safe and easy to put back if you ever wanted to, but they're the two remaining things slowing you down.

**What "Data Saver" means:** it's a setting that deliberately restricts your data in the background — apps can't refresh behind the scenes, and things can feel slow or just not load. It's useful if someone is desperately trying to save data, but you have plenty left (8.7 GB used out of 15 GB), so there's no reason to have it on.

---

**Step 1 — Turn Off Data Saver**

1. Open **Settings**.
2. Tap **Network & internet** (or "Connections").
3. Tap **Data Saver** (it may be under "Data usage").
4. Switch it **Off**.

You'll find that quicker in your quick settings too: swipe down twice from the top and see if there's a "Data Saver" tile you can just tap once to grey it out.

*(On an iPhone this is called "Low Data Mode": Settings → Cellular → Cellular Data Options → Low Data Mode → Off.)*

**Step 2 — Change the Network Mode off 2G**

1. Open **Settings**.
2. Tap **Network & internet** (or "Connections").
3. Tap **Mobile network** (or "SIMs" / "Mobile Data").
4. Tap **Preferred network mode** (or "Network mode").
5. Pick the option that mentions **5G** or **4G/LTE** — commonly written as **"5G/LTE preferred"**, **"5G/4G/3G/2G auto connect"**, or **"LTE (recommended)"**.

*(On an iPhone: Settings → Cellular → Cellular Data Options → Voice & Data → 5G Auto or LTE.)*

Just make sure you don't pick anything that says "2G only" or "3G only" — those are the slow ones.

---

Please try both of those and then tell me:
- What does it say at the top now — still 2G, or **5G / LTE / 4G**?
- Is the **Data Saver** message gone?
- How many **bars** do you see, and does a webpage load now?

On the single bar: once the phone gets off 2G this may well improve on its own. But if you're still on one bar afterwards, tell me where you are at the time (at home, at work, out and about) and roughly where in the building — one bar usually means the signal is struggling to reach you indoors, and there are a couple more things we can try for that.
turns.execution_output: User: Alright, I'll try the data saver one first. One thing at a time, if that's alright.

turns.thought:
That's a big difference — you've done it! Now let me check things on my side and help you properly test the speed.

**What you've fixed:**
- ✅ Airplane Mode → off (that was cutting you off completely)
- ✅ Mobile data → on (that's why the internet wouldn't work at all)
- ✅ Network mode → 5G instead of 2G (that's why it crawled when it did work)
- ✅ Data Saver → off (that was throttling things in the background)

And you've gone from one bar to four, which is an excellent signal. On the account side I can confirm your line 555-123-2002 is Active, you've used 8.7 GB of your 15 GB allowance so there's no data limit slowdown, and roaming is already enabled should you travel.

**Now, let's test it properly.** I don't have a speed test I can run on your phone from here, so please do this yourself — it's the real proof:

1. Make sure **Wi-Fi is off** for the test, so we know it's the mobile network doing the work. (Swipe down twice from the top and tap the Wi-Fi tile so it goes grey.)
2. Open your web browser and load a page you don't visit often — maybe a news site.
3. Then, if you like, open Google and type **"internet speed test"** and tap the **"Run Speed Test"** button — that gives you an actual number.

**Tell me what you find, and we'll know for sure:**
- Did the webpage load, and did it feel quick or still sluggish?
- If you ran the speed test, what download speed did it show?
- Try a picture message to someone as well — with 2G those simply couldn't send, but on 5G they should go through fine.

If it's still slow even on 5G with four bars, don't worry — there are a few more things we can look at, so just let me know and we'll keep going. But honestly, from everything you've described, I'd expect it to be working well now. Go on, give it a try!
turns.execution_output: User: Let me check that the Wi-Fi is off first, and then I'll run that speed test.

turns.thought:
You're all set — 275 Mbps and "Excellent" is exactly what we wanted to see, and with Wi-Fi off that's genuinely your mobile data doing the work. From no signal at all to full-speed 5G in a few minutes. You did great following those steps.

To answer your question directly: **nothing else is needed for the mobile data issue.** There's no lasting damage from any of it — you'd just accidentally switched Airplane Mode on, and the phone had also fallen back to 2G with mobile data and Data Saver restricting things. All four are now set the way they should be.

For future reference, the quick way to remember it: if your internet ever stops again, first check that **no airplane symbol** is showing at the top of your screen, and second, that the network says **5G / LTE / 4G** and not 2G. That covers the vast majority of cases.

Two small things I noticed on your account while we were working, purely in case they matter to you — no need to act now:

- Your account has **three lines**. The number you called about (555-123-2002) is working fine, but one of the others (ending 2003) is currently **suspended**. If that's a line you or a family member uses, I can look into why and whether it can be restored.
- There's a **bill of $150 due on 19 February** that's still open. It isn't overdue yet, so nothing is wrong — but I can send you a payment request for it now if you'd like to get it settled early.

Happy to help with either, or just leave everything as it is. Otherwise, enjoy the fast internet — glad we got you sorted!
